DESCRIPTION: FIND — `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()` never checks that each proof belongs to the corresponding exported record. Location: `bench/evidence.py`, `verify_bundle()`. Evidence: the loop calls `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)` but does not compare `proof["chain_hash"]` against `record["chain_hash"]`. In `verification_chain.py`, `verify_inclusion_proof()` validates only the proof’s internal `chain_hash` and Merkle path against the root; it does not consume the exported record. Therefore a tampered bundle can pair record A with proof for record B and still pass verification as long as proof B is valid under the root.
FOLLOW: This breaks the core “self-contained bundle” contract. `export_bundle()` emits parallel `records` and `inclusion_proofs`; `verify_bundle()` is supposed to verify all proofs in the bundle, but currently only proves that some chain member exists for each proof, not that the attached record is that member. Any consumer trusting `verify_bundle()` can be shown authentic proof material next to substituted record content, producing silently misleading audit output. The zip-length bug in C0009/C0018 is separate; even with equal lengths, record/proof mismatches remain undetected.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `trace_finding()` only returns records already indexed by finding ID and therefore omits related provenance records that do not themselves mention the finding. Location: `bench/evidence.py`, `trace_finding()`. Evidence: the method starts with `indices = self._index.by_finding.get(finding_id, [])` and never follows cross-references. Yet the module docstring and task description claim cross-referencing to “the policy that was active, the health scan from that round, and the verdicts it received,” and the trace docstring says “Returns every event related to this finding ID.” Policy snapshots for the same round typically do not embed `C####`, so they can never appear in the trace despite `_classify_event()` having dedicated `policy` and `health_scan` event types.
FOLLOW: Provenance traces are systematically incomplete: a finding trace contains direct mentions only, not the round-context records the module claims to surface. This also weakens `export_bundle(finding_id=...)`, which relies on the same finding index and will omit contextual records needed for external audit. The bug is completeness/semantic mismatch, not ordering. Existing finding-ID extraction fixes do not solve it because policy snapshots and some health scans may legitimately not mention the finding text.
